**Most Famous American Composers (by era)**  

| Era | Composer | Notable Works / Contributions |
|-----|----------|--------------------------------|
| **Classical/ Romantic** | **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| | **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man*, *Rodeo* |
| | **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | *West Side Story*, *On the Town*, *Candide* |
| | **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalist works: *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *Koyaanisqatsi* |
| | **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film scores: *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* |
| | **Ludwig van Beethoven** (not American) – *N/A* | (Just to note he’s not an American composer) |
| **Contemporary/ Pop** | **Kurt Cobain** (not a composer in classical sense) – *N/A* | (Just to note he’s not a composer in classical sense) |
| | **Bob Dylan** (born 1941) | Songwriting: *Blowin’ in the Wind*, *Like a Rolling Stone* |
| | **Prince** (1958‑2016) | *Purple Rain*, *1999* |
| | **Taylor Swift** (born 1989) | *Love Story*, *Shake It Off* |
| | **Beyoncé** (born 1981) | *Crazy in Love*, *Halo* |

> **Key Takeaway:**  
> The United States has produced a wide spectrum of composers—from classical giants like Gershwin and Copland to modern film score legends like John Williams, and even pop icons whose songwriting has shaped contemporary music. The “most famous” can vary by genre, but the names above are consistently cited as the most influential and widely recognized.
